title: Crime Bill puts burden on company Directors: BASL | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 22 October 2026 00:00
-     - 24

The Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill (OCB) requires a company Director to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that an offence by the company was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised due diligence, the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) said yesterday.

The BASL said the Bill also sets aside the rules that make confessions to police officers inadmissible, allows statements signed by an accused in police custody to be proved against him, and denies persons sentenced under it eligibility for any early release scheme.

“These provisions erode the principle that a person is presumed innocent until proven guilty and, together with the detention regime, amount to an overreach by the Government that threatens the freedoms of association and movement and the liberty of the citizen,” the BASL said.

The OCB classifies as “serious crimes” all offences punishable by imprisonment of four years or more, together with approximately 50 offences listed in its First Schedule. These include copyright and trademark infringement, excise and forest offences, and gambling licensing offences. The Bill’s extraordinary powers apply where such an offence is committed by a member of an “organised criminal group”, meaning a structured group of three or more persons acting in concert to obtain a financial or other material benefit. The group need not have formal roles, continuity of membership or a developed structure.

“These provisions would appear to be far broader than anything required to combat organised crime,” the BASL said.

A person may be arrested and held on a Detention Order issued by the Secretary to the Ministry of the Minister to whom the subject of the Sri Lanka Police Force is assigned. The Magistrate is bound to give effect to the order, for periods of up to two months at a time and up to one year in all, with bail available only from the High Court.

“At no stage before the order is issued does a court decide whether detention is necessary. In effect, the OCB seeks to bypass the judicial process in arresting and detaining persons for any offence of this breadth,” the BASL said.

The BASL said there was no public consultation in the preparation of the OCB, and that it was neither consulted nor informed of its drafting.

On the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA), the BASL said the Bill as gazetted departs significantly from the draft approved by the Committee appointed to review the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).

“The BASL’s nominees have informed the BASL that these changes were not referred back to the Committee or brought to the attention of its Chairman or members before publication,” it said.

The BASL has filed a Special Determination Application before the Supreme Court under Article 121 of the Constitution against the PSTA. It has called on the Government to withdraw the PSTA in its present form and to withdraw the OCB.

title: Standard Chartered Platinum Sponsor of Daily FT–UoC MBA Alumni Association Post-Budget Forum | Daily FT

Standard Chartered Sri Lanka CEO Bingumal Thewarathanthri (second from left) handing over the sponsorship cheque to University 

of Colombo MBA Alumni Association President Thantrige Supeshala (centre). Others from left: Standard Chartered Sri Lanka Head of Corporate Affairs, Brand and Marketing Kumudu Munasinghe, University of Colombo MBA Alumni Association Vice President Nilanka Abeywickrama and Executive Committee Member Pavithra Samarasinghe - Pic by Daminda Harsha Perera

Standard Chartered Sri Lanka has once again partnered the Daily FT and the University of Colombo MBA Alumni Association’s annual Post-Budget Forum as Platinum Sponsor. 

The forum, themed ‘See Things Clearly’, will discuss the potential impacts, opportunities and challenges of the 2027 Budget for businesses and individuals.

It will be held on 13 November, 2026 from 1.30 p.m. at Cinnamon Grand Colombo.

Standard Chartered Sri Lanka CEO Bingumal Thewarathanthri said: “Sri Lanka’s economic outlook presents a significant opportunity to accelerate sustainable growth, attract investment and strengthen competitiveness. As Platinum Sponsor of the Post Budget Forum 2027, Standard Chartered is proud to support an important platform for dialogue on the policy priorities and reforms that will shape the country’s next phase of growth. We remain committed to partnering our clients and stakeholders as Sri Lanka continues its journey towards long-term economic resilience and prosperity.”

At the forum, Secretary to the Treasury Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma will deliver the keynote followed by a panel discussion involving Advocata Institute Chairman Murtaza Jafferjee, Standard Chartered Bank Sri Lanka CEO Bingumal Thewarathanthri, A. Baur and Company Managing Director/CEO Rolf Blazer and Selyn Group of Impact Companies Chief Growth Officer Selyna Peiris. It will be moderated by Daily FT Editor/CEO Nisthar Cassim. title: NCPI unchanged at 8.1% in Sept. | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 22 October 2026 00:21
-     - 13

National inflation held steady at 8.1% year-on-year (YoY) in September 2026, unchanged from August, as higher food prices offset a decline in non-food costs, according to the latest National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) data released by the Department of Census and Statistics (DCS) yesterday.

The NCPI (Base: 2021=100) rose to 224.2 points in September from 223.9 in August. That was a month-on-month (MoM) increase of 0.3 index points or 0.11%, the smallest monthly rise of the year, and corresponds to a rise of Rs. 123.85 in the expenditure value of the market basket.

The September reading halts a run of six consecutive monthly increases in YoY inflation, which had climbed from 1.6% in February to 8.1% in August. The 12-month moving average kept rising, however, reaching 4.5% from 4.1% in August. This smoother gauge compares the average index over the past 12 months with that of the preceding 12 months.

Food inflation rose to 6.9% YoY from 6.6% in August, its highest in at least a year, while non-food inflation eased to 9.1% from 9.3%. Non-food items nonetheless remained the larger driver of the headline rate, contributing 5.00 percentage points to the 8.1% figure, against 3.11 percentage points from food.

Within non-food, Transport was the biggest single contributor, adding 2.20 percentage points to annual inflation. Petrol alone accounted for 1.05 percentage points, followed by Bus Fare at 0.36, Transport for Schooling/Preschooling at 0.19 and Diesel at 0.17. Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas and Other Fuels added 1.17 percentage points, led by Housing Rent (0.46 points), Materials for Maintenance (0.30 points) and LP Gas (0.23 points). Restaurants and Hotels (0.51 points), Education (0.34 points) and Miscellaneous Goods and Services (0.28 points) also contributed.

On the food side, the annual increase was driven by Fresh Fish (0.64 points), Dried Fish (0.42 points), Big Onions (0.39 points), Vegetables (0.32 points) and Green Chillies (0.28 points). Declines in Coconuts (-0.48 points) and Rice (-0.23 points) partly offset these gains.

On a MoM basis, food items added 0.19% to the index, while non-food items subtracted 0.08%.

title: SriLankan Airlines denies cyberattack claims | Daily FT
summary:
Thursday, 22 October 2026 00:20
-     - 11

SriLankan Airlines yesterday categorically denied recent media reports and public statements alleging that its Information Technology (IT) systems were hacked, hijacked or otherwise compromised, or that the airline is under the control of hackers.

The claims relate to an externally published cyber allegation on 29 June 2026 claiming that SriLankan Airlines’ IT systems had been breached.

Upon becoming aware of the claim made on 29 June 2026, SriLankan Airlines immediately undertook the necessary investigations, technical assessments and precautionary measures.

Based on the findings, no unauthorised access to the airline’s internal Information Technology environment or operational systems, compromise of information assets, unauthorised extraction of data, or disruption to the airline’s services or operational continuity was established.

The airline further confirms that its systems and services, including email services, have remained operational without disruption, with no impact on the airline’s operations or continuity of service at any point.

SriLankan Airlines also confirms that no ransom demand, whether in Bitcoin, U.S. dollars or any other form, has been received from the alleged party, and no negotiations relating to a ransom have taken place.

Accordingly, SriLankan Airlines categorically rejects allegations that its systems have been taken over or remain under the control of hackers.

SriLankan Airlines remains committed to safeguarding its information systems and ensuring the continued reliability of its services for passengers, employees and business partners.
